notes:
BMW i3 and i3s (I01), read over the CAN pair on the OBD-II socket.

Units are reached with ISO 15765-2 extended addressing: requests on CAN identifier 0x6F1 with the unit's address as the first data byte, replies on 0x600 plus the address starting with the tester address 0xF1 (docs/vehicles/bmw-mini.md).

The address table is transcribed from the transmit and receive identifiers in the Open Vehicle Monitoring System's read-only i3 module, developed against a 2018 i3s and polling these units with UDS ReadDataByIdentifier under extended addressing. The source says the car answers over the OBD-II port with the ignition on and for about 40 seconds after it is switched off or woken, and that the alarm sounds if anything is left plugged into the port when the car is locked. Treat every row as unconfirmed on a given car until `obd-read probe` shows the unit answering.

The bus is 11-bit CAN at 500 kbit/s. The default session, which every UDS unit must accept, is the one opened.
